latest_commit.subject: spec 2.34: §4A.6 documents the LIVE Simple-P regulator + skip ladder, not the retired PID
latest_commit.body:
Owner report: the board-config regulator tables described the ULP 1.2.4
positional PID, which has not been the operational law since the
Simple-P 16-tick regulator landed. The section now documents what
actually runs, with every value read from source:

Simple-P: N=16 encoder pulses per measurement, 1 % deadband, power
ceiling 4095, per-pump kp (step_per_pct) AC 6 / BP 10, max-error clamp
AC 30 % / BP 50 %, power floor 20 both — and the law stated plainly
(pwr += err% x step_per_pct, no integral, no derivative,
saturate-and-continue).

NEW table for the adaptive skip ladder and spin-up kick: the per-pump
ladders (AC 0,2,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024; BP
0,4,8,16,24,64,128,256,512,1024), skip_max 9 and skip_good 2 both,
DAC_START_AC 700 / DAC_START_BP 3200, escalate step 200 with decay on a
successful start, and the standing rule that one MOTOR_START_FAIL_AC
per boot/recovery is EXPECTED by design because the AC deliberately
starts below its ~1900 break-away so the device learns its start power.

The PID gains are demoted to an explicit LEGACY note — they remain in
board_config.py for the legacy run_pid path (BP dosing/parking history,
Control App test modes) and must not be read as the live tuning.

Sources: esp32/pump_regulator/main/ulp/main.c (op_p_*/ac_p_*/bp_p_*,
skip tables, DAC_START_ESCALATE_STEP) and fluispotter/board_config.py
(DAC_START_AC/_BP, SPR targets). .docx regenerated, Drive copy updated.
verify: 176 requirements, 153 PASS / 0 FAIL; spec-version gate sees 2.34.
